6416.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂er-dʰrom, from *h₂er- (“to fit”) + *-dʰrom (“tool or instrument suffix”), synchronically analyzable as ἀραρίσκω (ararískō) + -θρον (-thron).

6400.t: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂(e)rmós, from the root *h₂er- (“to fit together, join”), whence also ἀραρίσκω (ararískō, “join, fit together”).

6406.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂éḱmō. Cognates include Sanskrit अश्म॑न् (áśman), Avestan 𐬀𐬐𐬨𐬀𐬥 (akman), Old English hamor (English hammer), and Lithuanian akmuõ.

6422.t: From an earlier *ἄϝεθλον (*áwethlon), traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂weh₁- (“to blow (of wind)”) + *-dʰlom (forms nouns denoting tool or instrument), as if "gasp, pant, wheeze", if not from a similar root meaning "to strive".

6415.t: Contracted from ἀέρδην (aérdēn), from the root of ἀείρω (aeírō, “to lift”) + -δην (-dēn, deverbal adverb suffix).

6488.t: From ἔνθα (énthă, “there; where”) + -δε (-de, “here”, denoting motion towards the topic or speaker).

6413.t: Commonly derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éntm̥, accusative singular of *h₂énts. Alternatively, Dunkel suggests a 'directive' *h₂ént-o from the same root noun, with subsequent alpha harmony in Greek.

6401.t: From ἀγρός (ăgrós) + οἰκέω (oikéō). For the opposition with ἀστεῖος (ăsteîos), compare typologically Latin agrestis (cognate via Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵros), pāgānus, rūsticus vs. cīvīlis, urbānus.

6410.t: Probably cognate with ἄκρος (ắkros), but Beekes considers this uncertain.

6417.t: From ἀ- (a-, privative alpha) + ῥώννυμι (rhṓnnumi, “to strengthen”) + -τος (-tos).

6402.t: Generally considered to be a perfect participle of verb ἄγω (ắgō, “to lead”), but without the reduplication.

6471.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁el-nó-s, from *h₁el- (“deer”). Compare ἔλαφος (élaphos, “red deer”), Lithuanian elnias (“deer, stag, hart”), Russian оле́нь (olénʹ, “deer”), Russian лось (losʹ, “elk”), Old Armenian եղն (ełn, “hind”).

6443.t: Unknown. Not related to ἐγκεράννυμι (enkeránnumi, “to mix”).

6468.t: From ἐκτυπόω (ektŭpóō, “to model or work in relief”) + -μα (-ma, result noun suffix).

6408.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + κριτός (krĭtós, “chosen, picked out, separated”).

6414.t: From the same substrate root as ἄπιον (ắpĭon, “pear”) and Latin pirum (“pear”).

6405.t: From ἆθλος (âthlos, “conflict, struggle”) + -ιος (-ios, “a suffix added to nouns or adjectives, forming adjectives: pertaining to, belonging to”)

6430.t: From Ἀρσίνοος (Ărsĭ́noos) + -η (-ē, feminine noun-forming suffix), but by surface analysis, αἴρω (aírō, “to raise; to lift; to elevate”) + -σις (-sĭs) + -η (-ē).

6412.t: From ἀμφι- (ămphĭ-, “on both sides”) + ὁδός (hodós, “way; path”).
